post.description:
Submits a monthly identification file for a given platform. The file must follow the DPID format and naming convention (e.g. `DPID_4300001_2026-05_001.xml.gz`).

Once uploaded, the file is queued for asynchronous processing by Urssaf. The returned `urssafRef` uniquely identifies this submission and must be used to poll the processing status via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/identifications/{urssafRef}`.

**Business rules:**
  - The upload window is constrained by the identification calendar period. Uploads
    outside this window may be rejected.
  - Only one identification file per platform per period should be submitted.
  - The platform must have production access enabled to submit files outside of
    sandbox mode.

parameters.description: Describe the expected language in the results
parameters.name: Accept-Language

requestBody.description: Identification file submitted as `multipart/form-data`. The `name` field must follow the DPID naming convention and the `data` field must contain the binary content of the compressed XML file.

200.description: File successfully received and queued for asynchronous processing. The `urssafRef` returned must be retained to track the processing status of this submission.

get.description:
Returns the details and current processing status of an identification file submission, identified by its unique Urssaf reference.

The `status` field reflects the processing state of the file on Urssaf's side:
  - `IN_PROCESS`: the file has been received and is being processed.
  - `ACCEPTED`: the file has been successfully processed. Result files are
    made available depending on the submission content (see below).
  - `REJECTED`: the file was rejected. The global report details the reasons
    for rejection and is available for download.


**Result file availability:**
  - `globalReportRef`: always produced, whether the file is accepted or rejected.
  - `detailedReportRef`: produced only when the file is accepted.
  - `usersAnomaliesReportRef`: produced only when the file is accepted and at
    least one declared user has anomalies.
  - `affiliatedUsersFileRef`: produced only when the file is accepted and at
    least one user falls within the scope of the scheme.


All result files can be downloaded via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/identifications/{urssafRef}/file/{fileRef}`.

**Note:** Processing is asynchronous. Consumers should poll this endpoint after upload until the status transitions out of `IN_PROCESS`.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of identification file submissions for a given platform, ordered according to the `sort` parameter. Results can be filtered by withholding period using the `start_date` and `end_date` parameters.

Each item in the list is the full `Identification` object, identical to what is returned by `GET /platforms/{platformId}/identifications/{urssafRef}`. This includes the current processing status, submission metadata, statistics, and all available result file references (`globalReportRef`, `detailedReportRef`, `usersAnomaliesReportRef`, `affiliatedUsersFileRef`).

Result files can be downloaded via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/identifications/{urssafRef}/file/{fileRef}`.

**Note:** This endpoint returns all submissions regardless of their status (`IN_PROCESS`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`).

post.description:
Submits a declaration or regularisation file for a given platform. The `type` query parameter determines which type of file is being submitted, as each type follows a distinct interface contract and must comply with its corresponding XSD schema:
  - `DECLARATION`: a main declaration file covering a single withholding month.
    Must follow the DPDE XSD. The submission window is constrained by the
    declaration calendar period.
  - `REGULARISATION`: a regularisation file that can cover one or more
    withholding months. Must follow the DPRE XSD. A regularisation file can
    be submitted at any time, outside of any calendar constraint.


Once uploaded, the file is queued for asynchronous processing by Urssaf. The returned `urssafRef` uniquely identifies this submission and must be used to poll the processing status via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/declarations/{urssafRef}`.

**Business rules:**
  - Only one `DECLARATION` and one `REGULARISATION` can be in process at a time
    for a given platform. If a new file is submitted while one of the same type
    is already being processed, the API will accept the upload, but the
    processing system will reject it and produce a global report with a specific
    anomaly detailing the reason.
  - The platform must have production access enabled to submit files outside of
    sandbox mode.

parameters.description: ID of the platform
parameters.name: platformId

parameters.description: Describe the expected language in the results
parameters.name: Accept-Language

parameters.description: Type of file being submitted. Determines the applicable XSD schema and business rules. Use `DECLARATION` for a main monthly declaration file, or `REGULARISATION` for a corrective file covering one or more past periods.
parameters.name: type

requestBody.description: Declaration or regularisation file submitted as `multipart/form-data`. The `name` field must follow the appropriate naming convention (DPDE for declarations, DPRE for regularisations) and the `data` field must contain the binary content of the compressed XML file.

200.description: File successfully received and queued for asynchronous processing. The `urssafRef` returned must be retained to track the processing status of this submission. A `200` response does not guarantee the file will be accepted by the processing system — the final outcome must be checked via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/declarations/{urssafRef}`.

get.description:
Returns the details and current processing status of a declaration or regularisation file submission, identified by its unique Urssaf reference.

**File processing status (`status`):**
  - `IN_PROCESS`: the file has been received and is being processed by Urssaf.
  - `ACCEPTED`: the file has been successfully processed. Report files are made
    available depending on the submission content (see below).
  - `REJECTED`: the file was rejected. The global report details the reasons
    for rejection and is available for download.


**Report file availability:**
  - `globalReportRef`: always produced, whether the submission is accepted or rejected.
  - `detailedReportRef`: produced only when the submission is accepted.
  - `usersAnomaliesReportRef`: produced only when the submission is accepted and
    at least one declared user has anomalies.


All report files can be downloaded via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/declarations/{urssafRef}/file/{fileRef}`.

**Payment status (`paymentStatus`):**
  - `NOT_INITIATED`: no payment action has been taken yet. This is also the status
    reached when a previously initiated payment is cancelled (see below).
  - `DECLARED`: a bank transfer has been declared on the portal, but Urssaf has
    not yet received the funds. Transitions back to `NOT_INITIATED` if the
    declared transfer expires before Urssaf receives the payment.
  - `PROCESSING`: a PIS payment has been initiated on the portal, but Urssaf has
    not yet received the funds. Transitions back to `NOT_INITIATED` if the PIS
    payment fails.
  - `INTERLOCUTION`: the file was rejected due to a discrepancy between the
    contribution amount declared in the file and the amount received by Urssaf.
    A corrective file has been submitted, but the interlocution process with
    Urssaf is not yet finalised. The platform must either initiate contact with
    Urssaf if none has been made, or continue the ongoing exchange. Transitions
    back to `NOT_INITIATED` once the interlocution process is finalised.
  - `PROCESSED`: Urssaf has received a payment. If the file is still `IN_PROCESS`,
    it is not yet known whether the payment matches the declared amount. If the
    file is `REJECTED`, a discrepancy was detected between the file and the
    payment received. If the file is `ACCEPTED`, the full declaration flow is
    complete. Note that for regularisation files with no additional contribution
    amount due, `paymentStatus` transitions directly to `PROCESSED` without any
    payment action being required.


**Note:** `status` and `paymentStatus` are independent fields and must be read separately. Processing is asynchronous — consumers should poll this endpoint after upload until the status transitions out of `IN_PROCESS`.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of declaration and regularisation file submissions for a given platform, ordered according to the `sort` parameter. Results can be filtered by type and by withholding period using the `type`, `start_date` and `end_date` parameters.

Each item in the list is the full `Declaration` object, identical to what is returned by `GET /platforms/{platformId}/declarations/{urssafRef}`. This includes the current processing status, payment status, submission metadata, statistics, and all available report file references (`globalReportRef`, `detailedReportRef`, `usersAnomaliesReportRef`).

Report files can be downloaded via `GET /platforms/{platformId}/declarations/{urssafRef}/file/{fileRef}`.

**Declaration types:**
  - `DECLARATION`: a main declaration file covering a single withholding month.
  - `REGULARISATION`: a corrective file that can cover one or more withholding
    months.


**Note:** This endpoint returns all submissions regardless of their `status` (`IN_PROCESS`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`) or `paymentStatus`.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of notifications for a given platform, ordered by `newsDate` descending by default. The ordering can be changed via the `sort` parameter.

Notifications are generated automatically by the system to inform the platform of key events, such as a file being successfully uploaded or new report files becoming available. The `newsText` field is a human-readable message whose language is determined by the `Accept-Language` header.

Typical notification events include:
  - A file has been successfully uploaded (e.g. `"Your file DPID_... has been
    successfully uploaded."`).
  - New report files are available for a given submission (e.g. `"DPID_...:
    new reports available."`).


Sandbox notifications are prefixed with `"Sandbox"` in the `newsText` field, allowing the platform to distinguish between sandbox and production events.
